summary.text: 系 is interpreted in one paleographic account as a hand holding connected silk, suggesting binding or connection. Its early graphic analysis is disputed; later it is also used for lineage and in the current gloss “system.”

formation.text: The proposed hand-and-connected-silk interpretation describes a pictographic construction. The received Shuowen account instead analyzes 糸 as thread and 丿 as a sound element, while another proposal links 系 to 攣. These analyses remain unresolved. The selected seal-script image is a modern redraw and does not establish an evolutionary sequence.

components.text: 糸 is the thread or silk element in the received analysis and in the proposed picture of a hand holding connected strands.

history.text: The reported oracle-bone and bronze forms are interpreted as a hand holding connected silk. The received Shuowen parsing and a separate proposal linking 系 to 攣 differ from this account. The selected seal-script glyph is a modern redraw, not a dated artifact, and does not establish a sequence of forms.

系 is explicitly identified as a sound element within 係. Records also describe 系, 係, and 繫 as counterparts or variants in some contexts, but do not establish one graphic chronology or show that 系 regularly arose by simplifying 繫.

Reported early uses include ritual and place or state names, as well as a bronze personal name. A Warring States text is reported to use 系 for 奚; the evidence does not supply the older word’s sound or explain the choice of graph.

uncertainties.text: The proposed hand-and-silk picture, the received analysis of 糸 plus phonetic 丿, and the proposed link to 攣 remain competing accounts of 系’s graphic origin.
The reported ritual, place or state, and personal-name uses are not dated here as attestations of the lexical meanings thread, connection, lineage, or system.
The readings cited for 系 and 係 support a documented phonetic role for 系 in 係, but the distinct reconstructed forms do not resolve the precise historical sound relation.

senses.text: Thread is a recorded gloss and fits the interpretation of silk held by a hand. The evidence does not identify it as the earliest attested lexical use.
Binding or connection is the proposed sense of the hand holding connected silk. This is an interpretation of the graph’s origin, not a dated earliest use.

senses.period: historical; cited in a Han-dynasty text
senses.text: Connection is proposed to have extended to lineage; a Han-dynasty example is cited, but intermediate semantic stages are not documented.
System is a recorded modern gloss. Its historical development is not shown in this evidence.

senses.gloss: use of 系 to write 奚
senses.text: A Warring States use of 系 for 奚 is reported. This is a proposed graph borrowing for another word, not a meaning developing from 系; the old word’s sound and the sound match are not supplied.

developments.text: An extension from connection to lineage is proposed and illustrated with a Han-dynasty example, but intermediate stages are not documented.

limitations.text: The reported ritual, place or state, and personal-name uses are not established here as dated attestations of the listed lexical senses.
No chronology or semantic development for the modern gloss system is supplied.

items.period: Seal-script style; a modern redraw representing the received Shuowen seal form, not an excavated or dated artifact
items.caption: The seal-script form of 系 has a sweeping upper stroke above two enclosed loops and descending strokes. The graphic account of its earliest form is disputed: one interpretation sees a hand holding connected silk, while the received Shuowen analysis treats 丿 as phonetic.
items.alt: Black seal-script form of 系, with a sweeping upper stroke, two looped sections and descending strokes, on a white background.
items.selection_reason: This is the target character’s seal-script form and directly illustrates the disputed analysis of its upper component.
items.rights: Commons description marks the ancient-script representation public domain; modern vector redraw, not an artifact photograph.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; modern redraw of a received historical script form
items.caption: This seal-script form of 係 places a tall, narrow element beside the 系-like form. In the received analysis, 人 and 系 form 係, with 系 also serving as its phonetic; early forms are separately described as 人 with 糸, sometimes with hands.
items.alt: Black seal-script form of 係, with a tall narrow element on the left and a looped, branching form on the right, on a white background.
items.selection_reason: It helps explain the documented phonetic role of 系 within the related character 係 while showing that 係 has its own early graphic account.
items.rights: Commons file description states the SVG representation is public domain; modern vector redraw, not an artifact photograph.

limitations.text: These are modern redrawings of seal-script forms, not images of dated artifacts. The competing accounts of 系’s graphic origin remain unresolved, and these forms alone do not establish a chronological sequence.
